name: Constants in the language of Shakespeare
description: Shakespeare is a widely known esoteric programming language in which programs look like plays by Shakespeare, and numbers are given by combinations of ornate epithets. In this problem we will have a closer look at the way the numbers are described in Shakespeare. Each constant in Shakespeare is created from non-negative powers of 2 using arithmetic operations. For simplicity we'll allow only addition and subtraction and will look for a representation of the given number which requires a minimal number of operations. You are given an integer n . You have to represent it as n = a 1 + a 2 + ... + a m , where each of a i is a non-negative power of 2, possibly multiplied by -1. Find a representation which minimizes the value of m .
input_specification: The only line of input contains a positive integer n , written as its binary notation. The length of the notation is at most 10 6 . The first digit of the notation is guaranteed to be 1.
output_specification: Output the required minimal m . After it output m lines. Each line has to be formatted as " +2^x " or " -2^x ", where x is the power coefficient of the corresponding term. The order of the lines doesn't matter.
approach_summary: Express count as f(R) - f(L-1). Define memoized state dp[pos][tight][leading_zeros][cond] scanning digits from most to least significant in O(digits × base × states).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 132D — Constants in the language of Shakespeare [439. Digit DP]
topic_editorial.summary: Digit DP counting values in range $[L, R]$.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Counting valid integers in range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into $f(R) - f(L-1)$, where $f(X)$ counts valid integers in $[0, X]$. Numbers $\le X$ can be formed digit-by-digit from the most significant position. The constraint that the prefix does not exceed $X$ is tracked by a single boolean flag `tight`.
